questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted ti improve my French. Also, I wanted the opportunity to live and study in Paris because of all the cultural offers the city has.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Paris is an absolutely amazing city, and alone the chance to live here for four months made my experience amazing. The academic experience was at Dauphine was OK, but UCPH has a much higher academic standard.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The administration at Dauphine is very chaotic. All international students I spoke to had some kind of problem which needed to be solved out administratively upon arrival, and that created a lot of chaos and line in front of the international office. So honestly, it was not very easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There is an international office responsible for all the international students. I had to go there 3-4 times to solve out everything upon arrival. The staff at the international office give rather contradicting information, and they do not have the capacity to handle all the international students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: France is generally very chaotic when it comes to administrational stuff. Take it as an authentic experience. It will all work out in the end.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: You can apply through Dauphine housing service. They have some student dorms around the city. It was very easy, they sent me information about it via mail. My student dorm was placed in Bastille, which is a very nice and lively part of Paris. I was very satisfied with that location. My rent was cheap (400 €), and the dorm itself was also maybe not the best, but I think it lived up to my expectations for 400 € in a very nice area of Paris.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Dauphine does not offer on campus housing. And in general, it think the experience of Paris is better if you actually live in the city and have to build a daily life up yourself rather than living on a campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Paris is an amazing city to live in - enjoy it, go out, eat well!

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The course registration was in general a very frustrating and administratively difficult process. But again, my experience is that that is often how it is when you have to interact with an administration in France.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You apply to Dauphine through a link they send you. That proces was very easy. The course registration is more difficult. You chose courses also through a link they sent you, but a lot of courses time class, and the options for master courses in political or social science are not many. You can also change by going ditectly to the international office when you arrive

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can send an email to the international office before arrival, but they will most likely not respond. The easiest is to go there yourself when you arrive. As almost everyone have to change courses, it creates huge lines in front of the international office. I once waited in line for 1,5 hours.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not very succesful. I had problems finding relevant courses that were not time clashing. I ended up changing everything when I arrived, and I ended up taking a course in Finance to get it all to add up. In general, they do not offer so many master courses - especially not for political science students. You therefore have to take what you can get.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The courses are worth 3 or 6 ECTS, but the work load on the 3 ECTS-courses are sometimes the same as 6 ECTS-courses. Therefore, I would recommend to try to take as many 6 ECTS-courses as possible.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The academic level really varies across subjects.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses meant only for international students are not very good. The courses also open to French students at the actual master programmes are way better, but also more difficult. But in general, I think that UCPH has a higher academic level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It requires more participation in class. Often, your final grade is also based on assignments that you hand in throughout the semester.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
International Finance (3 ECTS)
International Politice (3 ECTS)
Management of Information Systems (6 ECTS)
Global Media (6 ECTS)
Industrial Organization (6 ECTS)
Global Climate Politics: Comparative EU-US Perspectives (6 ECTS)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Global Climate Politics was good. International Finance was very difficult, but I really learned a lot.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Going out! I ended up spending more money on going out than I had planned. There are so many good restaurants to chose from, and often social gatherings are centered around going out.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I don't know, I think in general prices are close to the Danish. Bakeries are a bit cheaper.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't use many, but Dauphine has a lot to offer.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are a lot of Erasmus events. It is a good way to meet people. And also, they had a welcoming week, which was unstructured, but a good way to meet people. They have an option to do sports as well. They have a lot of different student clubs as well.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to the Erasmus events (especially in the beginning) if you want to meet other international students. I went to a few, it was fun. Otherwise, I didn't use the non-academic options at school.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visit museums. Use the cultural offers in the city. Go to restaurants. Go out. Go to Versaille. Explore and enjoy the city, the options are so many!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: If you know some French you are better off.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really any.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The social lifestyle.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Prepare for a chaotic start
2) You have to take many courses as they are only worth 3 or 6 ECTS
3) The level of the courses and the work load really depends on whether you take courses from the actual master programmes or not

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You can take free French lessons without getting ECTS if you talk to the course administration or the French teacher.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The social aspect. And getting to know Paris.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The administrational stuff in the beginning.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Just enjoy Paris! I can't say hat enough times.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
